name: Cable Low-to-High Fly
summary: A standing cable fly variation where the arms pull diagonally upward and inward to target the clavicular head of the pectoralis major.

setup: Set both pulleys to the lowest position on a dual-cable station and attach single D-handles.
Grasp a handle in each hand with palms facing forward or slightly upward.
Step forward into a staggered stance to create tension on the cables, keeping the chest proud and torso upright with a slight forward lean.
steps: Start with arms extending down and slightly behind the torso, elbows soft with a slight fixed bend.
Sweep the hands upward and inward in a wide arc until they meet around chest to chin height.
Squeeze the upper chest firmly at peak contraction for a brief pause.
Slowly lower the handles along the same arc back to the starting stretch under control.
instructions.breathing: Exhale while sweeping the cables upward together; inhale as you slowly lower them back down.
cues: Lead with the inside of your elbows.
Keep the elbow angle locked throughout.

common_faults.fault: Bending and extending the elbows excessively, turning the fly into a bicep curl.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a fixed, slight bend in the elbows from start to finish.

common_faults.fault: Using excessive body swing and momentum from the hips to heave the weight up.
common_faults.correction: Brace your core, maintain a steady staggered stance, and use only shoulder movement.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders upward toward the ears at the top of the movement.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulder blades depressed and focus on driving the humerus across the upper chest.

precautions: Do not allow the cables to aggressively overstretch your shoulders behind your body at the bottom of the movement.
